hard_constraints: Talon Veyr is non-Force-sensitive; he navigates by prison habit, camera lag, and maintenance knowledge, not by the Force.
Ben Skywalker is a Jedi Knight; he may use Force sense to track Talon's route or sense pursuit, but the scene's primary navigation belongs to Talon.
The partnership is forced into existence through action; neither character has admitted it yet.
Talon's complaints are a mechanism to keep fear from becoming visible; do not have him articulate his fear directly.
Greyline adjusts pursuit when the expected escape route fails; this is a deliberate herding, not random pursuit.
The sea-wall route is exposed gantries above storm surf; it is the worst option and becomes the only option.
No Force abilities beyond basic Force sense; no lightsaber use in this scene.
No new plot mythology or exposition about Iresh, the holocron, or the Vigil in this scene.
Maintain commercial readability: goal, obstacle, movement, reversal, hook.
Do not write theme as thesis; put theme into behavior, pressure, cost, and consequence.
canon_risks: Risk of making Talon's prison knowledge feel like a Force ability; it must remain purely observational and experiential.
Risk of Ben using Force abilities that would be too showy or draw attention in a prison lockdown; keep Force sense subtle and internal.
Risk of the Greyline adjustment feeling omniscient; it should be explained by sensor feeds or motion tracking, not precognition.
Risk of Talon's complaints becoming random quips rather than fear-management; each complaint should serve the scene's tension or character.
legends_continuity_notes: Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works is a new setting for this novel; no prior Legends material describes it.
Greyline Strategic Services is a new organization; its operational methods (sensor tracking, real-time pursuit adjustment) are consistent with Legends-era private security firms.

The Galactic Alliance Guard (GAG) was dissolved after the Battle of Shedu Maad (41 ABY); Talon's prison knowledge comes from his GAG-era training and his years of imprisonment, not from any ongoing GAG infrastructure.
Storm conditions on a coastal prison world are consistent with Legends-era prison settings (e.g., Kessel, Spice Mines of Kessel).
possible_disney_bleed: Avoid any reference to 'Inquisitorius' as a post-Imperial organization; Legends Inquisitorius is Empire-era only.
Avoid 'World Between Worlds' or any Disney-canon Force concept.
Avoid 'kyber bleeding' or any Disney-canon lightsaber crystal lore.
Avoid 'Mandalorian' conventions from Disney canon (e.g., 'The Way'); Legends Mandalorians follow Resol'nare.
required_context_for_drafter: Talon Veyr was a GAG field agent under Colonel Maro Tess; his prison knowledge comes from that training and from years of imprisonment at Tarn Velos.
Ben Skywalker served in the GAG as a fourteen-year-old; he has some familiarity with GAG operational methods but not with Tarn Velos specifically.
Greyline is Tess's firm; the adjustment in pursuit indicates Tess or his operatives are reading the prison's sensors in real time.
The sea-wall route is exposed to storm surf and active pursuit; it is the worst option and becomes the only option.
Talon's complaints are a fear-management mechanism; he talks to keep fear from becoming visible.
The partnership is being forged through action; neither character has admitted it yet.
allowed_au_divergences: Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works is a new setting; its geography and security systems are original to this novel.
Greyline Strategic Services is a new organization; its operational methods are original.
Talon Veyr's backstory (Operation Glasshook, his reassignment, his imprisonment) is original to this novel.
The specific maintenance routes, camera lag patterns, and prison work-pattern knowledge Talon uses are original to this scene.
open_questions: What specific sensor or camera system does Greyline use to track Ben and Talon through the prison? (Drafter's choice; keep consistent with Legends-era technology.)
How many Greyline operatives are pursuing? (Drafter's choice; keep the threat level clear but not overwhelming.)
What is the exact layout of the sea-wall route? (Drafter's choice; ensure it is physically clear and dangerous.)
Does Ben use Force sense to detect the pursuit adjustment before Talon does, or does Talon read it from the prison's systems? (Drafter's choice; either is consistent with the scene's mission.)
